subject: Peak capacity smoothing & short-term quota uplift proposal
messages:
From: Eva Moreno <eva@tidalanalytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Quick question on temporary quota uplift for Q4 spike

Hey Marcus,

We expect a concentrated processing peak the week of Nov 23 as three of our customers run a scheduled reindex and live scoring job. That will push our token consumption roughly 6x our current daily average for about 5 days.

Before we start re-architecting, can Redwood provide a short-term quota uplift or a temporary higher rate limit that we can enable for that timeframe? We want to avoid throttling for customer-facing jobs. Also: what would the pricing look like for a 5–7 day uplift versus just paying overage per token?

I attached our high-level forecast. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Eva
Eva Moreno
Head of Data Products, Tidal Analytics

[a] Tidal Analytics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Eva Moreno <eva@tidalanalytics.com>
Cc: Harry Cole <harry@tidalanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on temporary quota uplift for Q4 spike

Hi Eva — thanks for the heads up and for the forecast. We can definitely help smooth that peak so your live scoring jobs don't hit throttles. Two practical paths we typically use: a short-term quota uplift with a blended uplift rate, or a consumption reconciliation mechanism where we bill the extra consumption at a pre-agreed uplift rate but cap peak latency via a temporary higher rate limit. Both keep your app responsive.

High level options (quick):
- 5–7 day temporary quota uplift: one-time fee calculated as expected incremental tokens * uplift rate; preserves your current SLA and avoids throttling.
- Temporary higher rate limit + reconciliation: increase concurrent tokens/sec limit for the window; bill actual extra consumption after the period at a slightly higher per-token price (we can offer a step-down discount if you commit to a larger monthly minimum).

If you can share the per-day token delta (the attached forecast helps), I can put numbers together today. If you'd like, we can also offer a conditional one-off discount if this spikes converts into committed growth in H1 next year.

Proposed next step: I’ll bring this to our finance and sales lead for sign-off on a short-term uplift price and a small conditional credit. Do you have any procurement deadlines?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
[attachment referenced: usage_history_q3.csv]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick question on temporary quota uplift for Q4 spike — need pricing sign-off

Ava / Priya — forwarding an ask from Tidal (attached forecast). They expect ~6x daily consumption for ~5 days starting Nov 23.

My recommended commercial approach:
1) Offer a 7-day "peak smoothing" uplift window with a blended uplift price of $0.0125 per extra token (instead of standard $0.02 overage) — this is effectively a limited-time concession to avoid throttles.
2) Alternatively, enable a temporary higher rate limit for concurrency (no change to per-token list price) and do a consumption reconciliation post-window at $0.015 per extra token, with a 10% credit if they commit to a 3-month incremental ARR target.

Pros/cons: uplift fee is simpler for procurement; rate-limit + reconciliation gives us flexibility and ties to commit. Want to be competitive without setting precedent for lower permanent pricing.

Attachments: tidal_q4_forecast.xlsx, usage_history_q3.csv

Can we approve the first option (7-day uplift at $0.0125) as a one-off for this account, and authorize a conditional 10% credit if they sign a 3-month incremental commit? If not, advise a counter.

—Marcus

Date: 2026-11-10T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick question on temporary quota uplift for Q4 spike — need pricing sign-off

Thanks for the context, Marcus. I’m okay with the 7-day uplift at $0.0125 as a one-off. Approve the uplift fee and authorize a conditional 10% credit if they commit to the 3-month incremental ARR target.

A couple of asks for finance & ops: make sure we set an explicit start/end timestamp in the order and include a post-window reconciliation so we can invoice just the incremental consumption. Also, put a cap so this uplift cannot be used as a long-term baseline (we should mark it "event-specific").

Ava

3) Operational notes: we will enable a temporary higher rate limit for the window so jobs do not get throttled; this will be disabled at the end timestamp automatically.
